hook: Why does dal take forever in Shimla?
hookSay: Why does dal take forever in Shimla? This free website lets you play with the science of Indian cooking.

beats.label: 1 · Heat & pressure
beats.say: Drag the heat from zero to {480|four hundred and eighty} degrees, and watch water molecules speed up as each change happens.

beats.label: Boiling point vs altitude
beats.say: Seal a pressure cooker, and water boils at about {116|one hundred and sixteen} degrees, even in Shimla. Open it, and it boils at just {92|ninety-two}.

beats.label: 2 · Spices & flavour
beats.say: {23|Twenty-three} spices, linked by the flavour molecules they share. Tap one to see its partners.

beats.label: 3 · Maillard & frying
beats.say: Brown an onion stage by stage, from raw to jammy, and see what changes inside.

beats.label: 4 · Dropping acid
beats.say: Cola sits at a {pH|P H} of {2.5|two point five}. Most balanced dishes sit between {4.3|four point three} and {4.9|four point nine}.

beats.label: 5 · Umami synergy
beats.say: Add dried mushroom to tomato, and the umami model jumps to about {29|twenty-nine} times.

beats.label: 6 · Modernist lab
beats.say: A microwave's {12|twelve} centimetre wave leaves cold stripes on a flat papad. Roll it in a glass, and it cooks evenly.

beats.label: 7 · Dish generators
beats.say: Pick a main ingredient and a regional style, and it builds the gravy, layer by layer.

beats.label: 8 · Biryani planner
beats.say: And plan a biryani as six tracks that run in parallel, ticking off each task.

outro: It's called Masala Lab Atlas: a free, fan-made companion to Krish Ashok's book, Masala Lab. The link is in the description.

end.title: Masala Lab Atlas
